caveats: All people, event records, conversations and analytics counts are synthetic. No production database or existing Docker data was reset.
The customer-site embedded preview is an original illustrative marketing component; the attendee screenshots and attendee film use the actual application with a real local backend.

Phone verification is disabled locally. SMS, SMTP delivery, payments, invoices, paid AI and moderation-provider calls are disabled and are not verified by these captures. The order wizard is not submitted.

The local Storage bucket holds only original public demo portraits. Signed original files are used locally because the hosted Pro image transformation endpoint is absent; private-bucket policy behavior is not demonstrated.

The isolated development snapshot uses the production single-mount lifecycle (reactStrictMode false). Its original development double-mount lifecycle dropped live UI handlers despite successful WebSocket delivery. No realtime handler or backend behavior was replaced.

Two existing development-only rendering warnings were corrected in the isolated snapshot: fetchPriority casing and deterministic particle rounding. Local image allowlist/CSP ports were adjusted for the isolated stack.
The source base schema overlaps two incremental migration statements. The already-existing publication membership and feedback policy were retained while subsequent migrations applied.

An existing notification heartbeat references pending_sms.dispatch_after, which is absent in the supplied schema. The notification/provider workflow is not verified; this does not affect the captured attendee or organizer requests.
The original demo portraits are 256-pixel assets; full-screen profile photos retain that source limitation.
verification: Real local Supabase stack with Postgres 17, Storage and Realtime; no fixture API implementation.
Original marketing page, event setup controls, attendee profiles and organizer analytics render against isolated data.
A profile like creates a reciprocal match through the real API.
The original chat UI sends a message; a separate authenticated browser receives it without reload and replies. Both messages survive reload and are present in local Postgres.
captureMethod: Original app operated through Playwright. Desktop screenshots use DPR 2; phone screenshots use DPR 3. The customer film uses lossless Chromium compositor PNG frames and the attendee film uses retina PNG frame capture. Final H.264 recordings have editorial English chapter bands outside the app pixels; the attendee recording preserves portrait orientation.

caveats: All numbers, people and contacts are fictional fixtures, not adoption or production performance evidence.
Marketing phone scenes and the organizer message preview are original authored illustrations, distinct from the real attendee app.
No order, payment, SMS, email or paid AI request was submitted. OTP funnel counts in the report are seeded stage data, not proof of delivered codes.

The client report PDF button did not download in the local browser. Its existing server PDF endpoint returned a document with missing numeric glyphs. The defective PDF is kept only in ignored QA evidence.
The client report hourly chart did not visibly render bars locally. Numerical report generation, funnel and audience breakdowns were verified; no repaired chart is presented.
CalendarView and AdminReliabilityView exist in source but are not imported by the current admin surface. They are source-only, not demonstrated navigation.
Guest self-deletion anonymizes personal fields but retains messages and other interactions for analytics; it is not immediate total erasure.
The organizer preview includes a misleading encryption badge despite an SMS disclaimer; the portfolio must not repeat it as an E2EE claim.

Prior local capture compatibility fixes are retained only in the isolated snapshot: local Storage image/CSP allowances, signed-original image fallback, fixed fetchPriority casing, deterministic particle rounding and dev StrictMode disabled to match production mounting. No product behavior was rewritten for these depth captures.
A Next.js development issue badge caused by the intentional offline test is hidden in final guest footage; the original product offline banner and retry/error states remain visible.
